title: Orphan Claim: Link policy to make it a regular claim (same record, land on Overview)
walkthroughSteps: Apply AC-01: lands on /fnol/search with a blank form. Type 'Jonas Kaufmann' into Client name and click Search. SK-2024-001 shows on the Claims tab without any state override.
On the Claims tab, open SK-2024-001's kebab menu and click 'Link policy' (renamed from 'Convert to claim' on 2026-09-22). The same 'Link policy' button sits on the claim's own Overview page.
The Link policy sheet lists policies for Jonas Kaufmann, each eligible or not ('Different client', 'Loss date outside policy period'). Click the eligible one (POL-2024-021).
A 'Link policy' confirm shows what changes (Skeleton state, Policy number, Broker). Confirm, then the 'Confirm loss location' sheet opens.
Lands on /claims/SK-2024-001 Overview. A toast says 'SK-2024-001 is now <new claim number>'. Same record, new regular claim number, the SK- number stays searchable.

There is no 'needs setup' banner any more. Instead a follow-up task lands in the handler's queue, and Close claim lists 'Converted orphan claim has no sections yet' and 'has no reserves set' as blockers until a section and a reserve exist.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Link policy links the policy onto the same claim record and lands on its Overview, no FNOL wizard
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
Clicking **Link policy** (from the Claims-tab kebab, or the button on the claim's own Overview page) opens a policy-picker sheet. Picking an eligible policy and confirming **updates the same claim record in place** (policy number, line of business, skeleton state *Awaiting policy* to *Linked*), gives it a regular claim number, opens *Confirm loss location*, then lands on `/claims/:id` Overview with a toast. No new claim is created and the FNOL wizard is never opened.

Jira (Feature / Requirement 9): *User should be able to convert an Orphan/ Skeleton claim into a regular claim.*

**NOTE [accepted-deviation]:** Confluence 3008228060 says conversion creates an incident record, completes the FNOL flow and calls CloseSkeletonClaim. The prototype updates the same record and skips FNOL. The screen differs from the source, pending product sign-off.

**NOTE [accepted-deviation]:** Confluence says an orphan can be linked to a customer or a policy. The prototype only links a policy. The screen differs from the source, pending product sign-off.

**NOTE [accepted-deviation]:** Jira says: "Only mandatory fields to create should be Date of Loss and Time of Loss". The orphan create form also requires Client name and Reason. The screen differs from Jira, pending product sign-off.

**NOTE [accepted-deviation]:** Jira says nothing about which policies are eligible. The prototype decides the rules "Different client" and "Loss date outside policy period". Not in Jira, pending product sign-off.

**NOTE [accepted-deviation]:** Jira says nothing about SLA handling. The "Days since" SLA column and the "Extend SLA" and "Abandon claim" menu items on the orphan list are made up by the prototype. Not in Jira, pending product sign-off.

**NOTE [accepted-deviation]:** Jira says nothing about closing a converted claim. The prototype blocks closure of a converted orphan until it has a section and a reserve (claim-closure-blocker.builder.ts). Not in Jira, pending product sign-off.

setup.description: SK-2024-001 is static seed data (claims.json) with status 'Awaiting policy', no state override needed. Search 'Jonas Kaufmann' manually, then use the real kebab action.
